findings.description: The producer path was under-specified because mailbox writes run in short-lived hook/CLI processes while the Codex MCP server is a separate long-lived stdio process. The plan needed a concrete trigger model instead of direct hook-to-server 'emit' wording.
findings.resolution: Reworked the producer into a Node.js stdio MCP server that watches durable actor state (`mailbox.json` plus manifest/review fields), writes a ready stamp after MCP initialization, performs startup catch-up only after the ready stamp exists, and emits deduped wakes per unread generation. Hooks no longer need direct IPC into the server.
findings.suggestedFix: Specify a watched durable-state producer and the dedupe boundary.

findings.description: The draft's 'new overlay helper/crate' wording ignored the existing Stage-A `codex-mcp-notification-bridge` crate and risked a redundant second bridge surface.
findings.resolution: The plan now extends `codex-rs-overlay/codex-mcp-notification-bridge` with a consumer module rather than proposing a second bridge crate.
findings.suggestedFix: Extend the existing Stage-A bridge instead of creating another overlay bridge crate.

findings.description: The queue-side consumer seam was not constrained tightly enough, making `realtime_text_for_event()` the most likely wrong implementation target.
findings.resolution: The plan now explicitly requires the consumer to live in the session event-dispatch path and forbids placing queue-side effects in `realtime_text_for_event()`; it cites the existing `async_watcher.rs:166-189` queue-then-wake precedent.
findings.suggestedFix: Prescribe the session event-dispatch seam and make the `realtime_text_for_event()` anti-pattern explicit.

findings.description: The Codex MCP config path and runtime shape were ambiguous. The plan used `.codex-plugin/.mcp.codex.json`, but Codex plugin manifests load `mcpServers` from a path string relative to the plugin root, and the server runtime/entrypoint were unspecified.
findings.resolution: The plan now uses plugin-root wiring (`"mcpServers": "./.mcp.codex.json"`), adds a plugin-root `launch.cmd`/stdio entrypoint, and states that the MCP server is a Node.js stdio process rather than a hook-side inline server.
findings.suggestedFix: Use root `.mcp.codex.json` plus a stable stdio launch entrypoint.

findings.description: Gate relaxation depended on a capability proof that had no concrete stamping site, and the file list omitted `hooks/actors.js`, where Codex launcher flags are emitted.
findings.resolution: The plan now makes `hooks/actors.js` part of US-003, requires it to launch codex members with `-c features.mcp_server_notifications=true`, and ties gate relaxation to a current-session ready stamp written by the MCP server after initialization succeeds.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the launcher seam and replace engine-only gating with a ready-stamp proof.

findings.description: The draft omitted required crews version/cache bookkeeping even though installed-path dogfood was an acceptance criterion.
findings.resolution: The plan now includes `scripts/bump-version.js`, `tests/version.test.js`, and an explicit acceptance criterion that version and marketplace stamps are updated in the same ship.
findings.suggestedFix: Call out the version-bump surfaces and make them part of the acceptance contract.

findings.description: The original 'exactly one wake' language was not testable because the dedupe unit was undefined and startup catch-up could race steady-state watch notifications.
findings.resolution: The plan now defines the dedupe boundary as one wake per unread generation keyed by `lastReviewRequiredSeq`, with startup catch-up emitted only after the current-session ready stamp exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Define the dedupe key and startup sequencing explicitly.

findings.description: Parallel Phase-1 development was fine, but merge activation of the producer needed a stronger rule so wakes are not emitted before the Codex consumer is available in the installed runtime.
findings.resolution: The producer cluster now states that `plugin.json` `mcpServers` activation should not land on main until the Codex consumer is installed and dogfood-ready, even if the code is developed in parallel.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate code development parallelism from merge-time activation.
